Have any of you had Laserdisc players? They were just so cool - at the end of their decadesong run they had THX sound and multiple versions of pure digital encoding. But originally Laserdisc were primitive digital encoding of video/analog recordings.

Near the end you could start to get used Laserdisc systems and libraries used from people who didn't want to get their money out of them, they had moved on to DVD and Blue-Ray - All in for the latest and greatest.

But I had all the Star Wars, multiple remasters. If I wanted cartoon Yoda that was accessible - if I wanted to see the original banding and artifacts around the Tie-Fighters and X-Wings, I could see that.

If I wanted to see that Storm Trooper bump his head on the Imperial Header, I could let the laser show me on repeat without degrading the disk.

And that was what it was a about. No degradation. This image is going to be perfect every time for the rest of my life and I need it to be that way.

Eventually I grew out of it.
